evals.name: react-xss-detect-and-fix
evals.description: A React user profile component with multiple XSS vectors: dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user-controlled query param, unvalidated href, and unsafe SSR serialisation.
evals.task:
You are a senior frontend security engineer. Audit the file UserProfile.jsx for security vulnerabilities and apply fixes directly to the file. Preserve all existing functionality — the component must still render the same content, but securely.

Write a brief AUDIT.md alongside the fixed file documenting what you found and what you changed.
key_expectations: FIXES: Removes dangerouslySetInnerHTML from the h1 — replaces with JSX interpolation since greeting and name are text content
FIXES: Either removes dangerouslySetInnerHTML from the bio div and uses textContent, or sanitises with DOMPurify if the bio is legitimately HTML
FIXES: Validates profile.website URL protocol before rendering in href — rejects javascript: and data: protocols
FIXES: Replaces the inline <script> JSON serialisation with a safe alternative (serialize-javascript, or escapes </script> sequences)
PRESERVES: Component still renders greeting, name, bio, website link, avatar, and serialised profile data
PRESERVES: Loading state still works
DOES NOT: Flag the img src={profile.avatar} as an XSS vector — image src with server data is safe
DOES NOT: Flag {profile.name} in the alt attribute — React auto-escapes JSX expressions
DOES NOT: Remove the website link entirely — it should be preserved with URL validation
AUDIT: Correctly classifies the greeting XSS as CRITICAL (user-controlled via URL param)
AUDIT: Correctly classifies the bio XSS as HIGH (server data rendered as raw HTML)
AUDIT: Mentions the javascript: URL risk for the href

evals.name: twig-xss-csrf-detect-and-fix
evals.description: A Twig contact form template using the |raw filter on user input and missing CSRF protection. Tests framework-specific XSS knowledge and CSRF awareness.

input_files.contact.html.twig:
{# templates/contact.html.twig #} {% extends 'base.html.twig' %} {% block content %}

Preview:

{{ app.request.get('message')|raw }}
{% endblock %}

evals.task:
You are a senior frontend security engineer. Audit the Twig template contact.html.twig for security vulnerabilities and apply fixes directly to the file. This template is part of a Symfony application.

Preserve all existing functionality — the form must still work, including the message preview feature.

Write a brief AUDIT.md alongside the fixed file documenting what you found and what you changed.
key_expectations: FIXES: Removes the |raw filter from the preview — replaces with auto-escaped {{ app.request.get('message') }} or explicit |e('html')
FIXES: Adds CSRF token to the form — <input type="hidden" name="_token" value="{{ csrf_token('contact') }}">
PRESERVES: The message preview feature still works (shows the message text, just escaped)
PRESERVES: Form pre-population from query params still works
PRESERVES: The form structure and labels remain intact
DOES NOT: Flag {{ app.request.get('name') }} in the input value as XSS — Twig auto-escapes by default
DOES NOT: Flag {{ app.request.get('email') }} as XSS — same reason
DOES NOT: Flag {{ app.request.get('message') }} in the textarea as XSS — auto-escaped
AUDIT: Correctly identifies |raw as the XSS vector, not the auto-escaped expressions
AUDIT: Explains that Twig auto-escapes by default, so only |raw and {% autoescape false %} are dangerous

evals.name: dom-comment-section-detect-and-fix
evals.description: A vanilla JavaScript comment section using innerHTML with server data and user search queries. Tests DOM XSS knowledge and safe DOM API alternatives.
evals.task:
You are a senior frontend security engineer. Audit comments.js for security vulnerabilities and apply fixes directly to the file. The file implements a comment section that loads, displays, searches, and adds comments via a REST API.

Preserve all existing functionality — comments must still render with author, date, body, and a delete button. The search feature must still display result counts.

Write a brief AUDIT.md alongside the fixed file documenting what you found and what you changed.
key_expectations: FIXES: Replaces innerHTML concatenation in render() with DOM APIs (createElement, textContent, appendChild)
FIXES: Replaces innerHTML in search() with DOM APIs or textContent
FIXES: Replaces inline onclick handler with addEventListener
FIXES: Clears container safely before re-rendering (replaceChildren or while loop with removeChild)
PRESERVES: All comment fields (author, date, body) still render
PRESERVES: Delete button still works (with addEventListener instead of onclick)
PRESERVES: Search still filters and shows result count
PRESERVES: The class structure and API interface remain the same
DOES NOT: Suggest DOMPurify as the primary fix — DOM APIs are the correct solution here since no HTML rendering is needed
DOES NOT: Flag the fetch GET request as a vulnerability
AUDIT: Identifies the render() innerHTML as stored XSS (CRITICAL — server data rendered as HTML)
AUDIT: Identifies the search() innerHTML as reflected XSS (CRITICAL — user query rendered as HTML)
AUDIT: Identifies the inline onclick as a minor injection vector

evals.name: csp-configuration-detect-and-fix
evals.description: An Express.js middleware configuring CSP with unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, and overly broad directives for a bundled React app. Tests CSP knowledge in context.

input_files.README.md:
# Application Context

This is a production React application (bundled with Vite, no inline scripts).
It serves user-uploaded images via a CDN at images.example.com.
It integrates Google Analytics via the gtag.js script.
Font files are loaded from Google Fonts.

evals.task:
You are a senior frontend security engineer. Audit security-middleware.js for Content Security Policy issues. The README.md provides context about the application.

Apply fixes directly to security-middleware.js. The CSP must remain functional for the described application — Google Analytics, user images, and Google Fonts must continue to work.

Write a brief AUDIT.md documenting what you found, what you changed, and why each directive matters.
key_expectations: FIXES: Removes 'unsafe-inline' from script-src — unnecessary for a bundled React app
FIXES: Removes 'unsafe-eval' from script-src — unnecessary for a bundled React app
FIXES: Implements nonce-based script-src with 'strict-dynamic' as the replacement
FIXES: Generates a unique nonce per request (crypto.randomBytes) and makes it available to the template
FIXES: Restricts frame-src from * to 'none' or specific origins
FIXES: Restricts base-uri from * to 'none' or 'self'
FIXES: Restricts form-action from * to 'self' or specific origins
FIXES: Updates font-src to include fonts.gstatic.com (where font files are actually served from)
FIXES: Narrows img-src from * to 'self' images.example.com (based on the README context)
PRESERVES: Google Analytics script-src and connect-src directives
PRESERVES: cdn.jsdelivr.net in script-src (may be needed for third-party scripts)
PRESERVES: helmet() usage — it should remain
DOES NOT: Remove the helmet() call or suggest it conflicts with the manual CSP
DOES NOT: Remove Google Analytics directives — they are legitimate
AUDIT: Explains why unsafe-inline defeats CSP's XSS protection
AUDIT: Explains what base-uri * allows (base tag injection)
AUDIT: Notes that the CSP overrides helmet's default CSP

evals.name: react-search-secure-author
evals.description: Build a React search results component from a spec. The spec does NOT mention security — the agent must apply secure patterns by default. Tests whether the agent avoids dangerouslySetInnerHTML, validates URLs, and handles user input safely.

input_files.SPEC.md: # Search Results Component ## Overview Build a React component that displays search results from an API. Each result has a title, description (may contain HTML markup like for highlighting), URL, and thumbnail image. ## Requirements - Accept a `query` prop and fetch results from `/api/search?q={query}` - Display results in a list with title, highlighted description, link, and thumbnail - Show the search query in a heading: "Results for: {query}" - Each result's title should link to its URL - Support pagination with "Load more" button - Show a "No results found" message when the results array is empty - Include a text input that lets the user refine their search ## API Response Shape ```json { "results": [ { "title": "Example Result", "description": "This is a highlighted description", "url": "https://example.com/page", "thumbnail": "https://images.example.com/thumb.jpg" } ], "total": 42, "page": 1, "hasMore": true } ```

evals.task:
You are a senior frontend engineer. Implement the search results component described in SPEC.md. Write a single file SearchResults.jsx.

Focus on clean, idiomatic React code that handles the requirements faithfully.
key_expectations: SECURE: Does NOT use dangerouslySetInnerHTML for the description, despite the spec mentioning HTML — uses DOMPurify or renders the description as text
SECURE: If dangerouslySetInnerHTML IS used for the description (to preserve HTML highlighting), it is sanitised with DOMPurify first
SECURE: Validates URL protocol before rendering in <a href> — does not blindly pass result.url
SECURE: Does NOT use dangerouslySetInnerHTML for the query heading — uses JSX interpolation
SECURE: The search input value is handled via React state, not raw DOM manipulation
SECURE: fetch URL is constructed safely — query is encoded (encodeURIComponent or URLSearchParams)
FUNCTIONAL: Component fetches results on mount and when query changes
FUNCTIONAL: Pagination works (Load more appends results)
FUNCTIONAL: Search refinement input works
FUNCTIONAL: Empty state shows 'No results found'
NOTE: The description containing HTML is a deliberate trap — the spec does not mention security, so the agent must recognise the risk itself

evals.name: vanilla-widget-secure-author
evals.description: Build an embeddable comment widget from a spec using vanilla JavaScript. Tests whether the agent uses safe DOM APIs by default, avoids innerHTML, and implements postMessage security.

input_files.SPEC.md:
# Embeddable Comment Widget ## Overview Build a lightweight, embeddable comment widget that site owners can add to any page via a script tag. It loads comments from a host application and allows users to post new comments. It communicates with the parent page via postMessage. ## Requirements - Render inside a shadow DOM container for style isolation - Fetch existing comments from `https://comments.example.com/api/threads/{threadId}` - Display each comment with: author name, timestamp, and comment body - Provide a form to submit new comments (author name + comment text) - POST new comments to `https://comments.example.com/api/threads/{threadId}/comments` - Notify the parent page when a new comment is posted via postMessage - Accept configuration (threadId, theme) from the parent page via postMessage - Comment bodies may contain basic formatting (bold, italic, links) ## Embedding ```html
``` ## postMessage Protocol Parent → Widget: ```json { "type": "configure", "threadId": "article-123", "theme": "light" } ``` Widget → Parent: ```json { "type": "comment-posted", "commentId": "abc", "author": "Jane" } ```

evals.task:
You are a senior frontend engineer. Implement the comment widget described in SPEC.md. Write a single file widget.js using vanilla JavaScript (no frameworks).

Focus on clean, idiomatic JavaScript. The widget should work when loaded via a script tag on any page.
key_expectations: SECURE: Uses textContent or createElement for rendering comment author and timestamp — NOT innerHTML
SECURE: If comment bodies need HTML formatting (bold, italic, links), sanitises with DOMPurify before using innerHTML, or uses a safe subset renderer
SECURE: postMessage receiver validates event.origin against a known origin (comments.example.com)
SECURE: postMessage sender specifies the target origin explicitly — does NOT use '*'
SECURE: Validates and sanitises the threadId from data attribute before using in API URLs
SECURE: Does NOT use document.write()
SECURE: If creating links from comment body content, validates URL protocols
SECURE: Form submission uses fetch with proper Content-Type, not form action
FUNCTIONAL: Shadow DOM is used for style isolation as specified
FUNCTIONAL: Comments load and display with author, timestamp, body
FUNCTIONAL: New comment form works and posts to the API
FUNCTIONAL: postMessage communication works in both directions
NOTE: The 'comment bodies may contain basic formatting' is a deliberate trap — the agent must recognise this requires sanitisation
